affectedPublicSurfaces: NO PUBLIC PRODUCT SURFACE, stated plainly rather than invented. This slice touches `.github/workflows/pr.yml`, `tests/unit/test_three_tier_ci_contract.py` and one paragraph of `CLAUDE.md`. Nothing it changes is imported by `backend/src/juli_backend/**`, served by any `/v1` route, bundled into `apps/**`, deployed by `release.yml`, or present in any runtime image. There is no candidate process to point a browser at, no seller-visible behaviour, and no migration.

The surface it DOES have is CI's own verdict on every issue-tier PR. Today `classify-tier` derives the tier from the BASE ref, so an issue PR based on `main` classifies `tier=main` and `artifact-retention-guard`, `validate-gates` and `merge-status` all SKIP. Verified SKIPPED on #1945, #1954, #1956, #1965 and #1975 - every PR in the W6 wave. A gate that never executes is indistinguishable from a gate that passed, which is exactly the Wave-2 silent-artifact-loss condition (ADR-079) the guard was written to make visible.

doNotInfer: THE SEQUENCING IS THE POINT AND IT IS ALREADY SATISFIED - do not re-litigate it, and do not widen anything further. Step 1 (PR #1976) merged; step 2 (ACs renumbered) done; step 3 (a genuine PASS status record) is satisfied by issue-1958.json. Widening any condition beyond the three jobs this issue names would red-line PRs that have no record and no way to get one.
pr.yml HAS ONE WRITER AT A TIME (CLAUDE.md). No other in-flight branch may edit it while this one is open.

EDITING pr.yml's `needs:` LISTS BY STRING REPLACEMENT IS A KNOWN TRAP: duplicate `- <job>` entries appear under several jobs, so a naive replace hits the wrong one. The silent symptom is an empty `needs.X.result`. Anchor every edit on the job header, and re-read the file after editing to confirm which block changed.

NEVER SATISFY A GATE BY EDITING GATE CONFIGURATION (ADR-095). This slice edits a trigger condition, which is legitimate; changing what the guard CHECKS, or adding an escape hatch so it passes without a record, is not.
This PR must go red on artifact-retention-guard before it goes green - that IS acceptance criterion 2 demonstrating itself. Do not try to avoid the red round; report it as the evidence it is.
A guard must be seen failing (.cursor/rules/code-quality.mdc): print what each new test collected, make it go red on purpose, report both.

AC5 removes the dormancy caveat from CLAUDE.md. CLAUDE.md is Tier-1 and tests/unit/test_ratchets.py pins tier1_always_on_tokens as must_not_rise - a removal lowers it, which is fine, but run the ratchet and report the number.
